articles.title: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) in children and adolescents : an analysis of 655 knees according to the CPAK classification.
articles.authors: Pott H, Savov P, Stauss R, Chen DB, MacDessi SJ, Ettinger M
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 4 to 18 years
articles.outcomes: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification phenotypes, hip-knee-ankle angle, and joint line obliquity measurements
articles.take_home: Most children and teenagers had similar overall knee alignment as they grew from age 4 to 18, but the angle of the knee joint surface changed noticeably with age. The study provides normal reference values for how knee alignment develops during growth.

articles.title: A Review of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures and Patient Demographics in Randomized Controlled Trials Used to Synthesize Clinical Practice Guidelines for Hip Fractures in Older Adults.
articles.authors: Valdivia LM, Farid CJ, Nguyen AX, Swaminathan S, Moucha CS, Hayden BL
articles.study_type: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Older adults with hip fractures in randomised controlled trials informing clinical practice guidelines
articles.outcomes: Reporting of patient language proficiency, race and ethnicity, use of patient-reported outcome measures and culturally adapted versions
articles.take_home: Most studies used to create hip fracture treatment guidelines do not report basic information about patients' language, race or ethnicity, and rarely use outcome measures that have been translated or adapted for different cultures. This means guidelines may not be representative of all older adults who have hip fractures.

articles.title: Association of Extended Oral Antibiotic Prophylaxis With 90-Day Complication Rates After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Propensity-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Haziza S, Greenberg M, Spagnuola J, Duchnycz R, Harbaugh T, Abdo ZE
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection, superficial skin infection, and revision surgery at 90 days postoperatively
articles.take_home: Patients who received extended oral antibiotics after knee replacement had higher rates of serious joint infection and need for revision surgery compared to those who did not, which was unexpected and contrary to the intended benefit. The researchers suggest further studies are needed to understand why extended oral antibiotics may not help prevent complications after knee replacement.

articles.title: Japanese Knee Osteoarthritis Measure at Two Weeks as a Key Predictor of Early Functional Recovery After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kugo M, Kumagai K, Taniguchi M, Kubo M, Sawano S, Ando K, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Japanese Knee Osteoarthritis Measure (JKOM) score, pain intensity, mobility tests, muscle strength, and balance performance at two and four weeks after surgery
articles.take_home: Measuring patients' recovery using the JKOM questionnaire at two weeks after knee replacement surgery helps predict how well they will recover at four weeks. Patients with higher pain levels and poorer movement ability early on are more likely to have slower recovery.

articles.title: Administration of Preoperative Cryoneurolysis is Associated with Continued and Persistent Opioid Reduction and Improved Outcomes in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Ng MK, Lin JH, Spitzer AI, Dasa V, Rivadeneyra A, Rogenmoser D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative opioid use, pain severity, and functional recovery scores at six months
articles.take_home: Patients who received cryoneurolysis before knee replacement surgery used fewer opioids after surgery and reported lower pain levels, with modest improvements in knee function at six months. This suggests cryoneurolysis, a cold therapy technique applied to nerves, may help reduce the need for pain medication after knee surgery.

articles.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients Who Have a Body Mass Index >/= 40: Outcomes at an Institution Without Cutoffs.
articles.authors: Salazar C, Shankar V, Hanna A, Levens B, Seref-Ferlengez Z, Lo Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Return to operating room, revision surgery, infection, and aseptic implant failure
articles.take_home: Patients with a BMI of 40 or more had higher rates of infection, unplanned return to surgery, and revision surgery compared to those with lower BMI. However, the study suggests that the increased risk is linked to both obesity itself and the additional health problems these patients often have, rather than BMI alone being a reason to refuse surgery.

articles.title: Complication Profile of A Computed Tomography-Guided Robotic-Arm Assisted Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty System: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Tse S, Lisacek-Kiosoglous AB, Lee P, Powling AS, Hagos A, Muhammad I, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (robotic-arm assisted or manual)
articles.sample_size: 10,894 robotic-arm assisted cases and 10,065 manual cases across 35 studies
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative, perioperative and postoperative complications including deep joint infection, additional procedures and prosthetic loosening
articles.take_home: Robotic-arm assisted knee replacement had fewer overall complications (3.8%) compared with manual surgery (5.5%), though differences in serious complications like infection were not statistically significant. Both approaches appear safe, but robotic surgery showed a trend towards fewer problems needing further treatment.

articles.title: Prognostic Prediction of Femoral Head Collapse Using Necrotic Size and Lateral Extent on Computed Tomography Images in Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head.
articles.authors: Otaka K, Osawa Y, Funahashi H, Takegami Y, Imagama S
articles.population: Patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head
articles.outcomes: Femoral head collapse of 3 mm or more; 5-year collapse-free survival rates
articles.take_home: Two measurements on CT scans (coronal vertical diameter ratio of 49% or more and lateral necrotic extent ratio of 90% or more) can help predict which patients with femoral head bone death are at highest risk of collapse. Patients with both measurements at these levels had a 100% risk of collapse, compared to only 9.5% in those with neither.

articles.title: Mitigation of Vascular Complications in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty with Intra-Pelvic Migration of Implants: A Pre-Operative Algorithmic Approach.
articles.authors: Kumar V, Kabra A, Behera A, Ojha MM, Shankar V, Gamanagatti S
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty for intra-pelvic implant or cement migration
articles.outcomes: Vascular injuries, blood loss, transfusion requirements, perioperative complications, and need for emergency conversion
articles.take_home: Using CT scans before surgery and blocking off blood vessels with catheters or coils in patients with migrated hip implants near major vessels reduced the risk of dangerous bleeding during revision surgery, with no major vascular injuries occurring in this group.

articles.title: The morphometric variability of the acetabular labrum: Insights for personalised hip labral reconstruction.
articles.authors: Capurro-Soler B, Gonzalez-VonderMeden S, Pizarro-Geraldo W, Gursoy S, Kocaoglu B, Chahla J, et al.
articles.study_type: Morphometric analysis of cadaveric hip specimens
articles.population: Adult hip specimens with normal hip anatomy and intact labral and cartilage structures
articles.outcomes: Labral height measurements in anterior, superior and posterior regions; transverse ligament width; acetabular diameter; comparison of measurements between males and females
articles.take_home: The hip labrum is thicker towards the back of the socket and thinner towards the front, with males having labra approximately 1 mm larger than females across all regions. These differences could help surgeons choose appropriately sized grafts when reconstructing damaged labrums.

articles.title: Do we need to use the largest possible size of the Proximal Femoral Nail Anti-rotation (PFNA) in well-reduced intertrochanteric fracture? A study of distal PFNA intramedullary canal occupying ratio (ICOR).
articles.authors: Tantavisut S, Amarase C, Rattanasermsub N, Artykbay S, Viriyakorkitkul S
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and above with unilateral intertrochanteric hip fractures treated with PFNA surgery
articles.outcomes: Bone healing assessed by Radiographic Union Score for Hip (RUSH) at 2, 6, and 12 weeks; fixation stability assessed by comparing radiographs immediately and at 3 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: The size of the nail used (measured by how much space it fills in the bone canal) did not affect how well the fracture healed or how stable the fixation was. Surgeons do not need to always use the largest possible nail size, as using a smaller nail did not lead to worse outcomes.

articles.title: Periprosthetic strain-adaptive bone remodeling of conservative metaphyseal fitting versus conventional anatomic cementless femoral stem.
articles.authors: Kim YH, Park JW, Jang YS, Kim EJ
articles.population: Patients younger than 50 years undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 168 patients with conservative metaphyseal-fitting stems (201 hips) and 181 patients with conventional anatomic stems (209 hips)
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic bone mass changes measured by DEXA, Harris Hip Score, WOMAC score, UCLA activity score, revision rates, and implant survival at 20-22 years
articles.take_home: Both types of hip stem worked very well over 20-22 years with similar survival rates of around 97%. However, the conventional stems caused more bone loss around the implant compared to the conservative metaphyseal-fitting stems.

articles.title: Short-term complications of open versus arthroscopic osteochondral allograft transplantation in the knee: a national database study.
articles.authors: Sribhashyam S, Chow AK, Chin RS, Whitaker S, Cuthbert AS, Cassidy BP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective national database analysis with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults undergoing elective knee osteochondral allograft transplantation
articles.outcomes: 30-day complications including adverse events, surgical-site infection, thromboembolism, transfusion, unplanned reoperation, hospital admission, operative time, and length of stay
articles.take_home: Both open and arthroscopic approaches to knee osteochondral allograft transplantation are very safe, with complication rates below 3% and no meaningful difference between techniques in the first month after surgery. Open procedures require longer operative time and hospital stay, likely because they are used for larger or more complex lesions rather than because of safety concerns.

articles.title: Fracture laterality as an independent prognostic factor for clinical outcomes after hip fracture surgery : an analysis of 72,008 patients.
articles.authors: Takegami Y, Imaizumi T, Sato K, Osawa Y, Funahashi H, Imagama S
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using administrative database
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary surgery for hip fracture in Japan between 2015 and 2023
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality and impaired independence in activities of daily living (Barthel index score less than 60) at discharge
articles.take_home: Right-sided hip fractures were associated with worse ability to perform daily activities after discharge compared to left-sided fractures. Right-sided fractures were also linked to higher death rates in hospital for patients with multiple other health conditions.

articles.title: Wear performance of metal and ceramic long-neck femoral head taper connections: an experimental ex vivo study.
articles.authors: Ribeiro de Sousa M, Neuvonen P, Saikko V
articles.population: Femoral head taper connections (metal and ceramic)
articles.sample_size: 36 mm diameter heads of long and extra-long neck types
articles.outcomes: Wear performance, metal release (Ti and Co), head disassembly forces, wear patterns, neck fracture incidence
articles.take_home: Long and extra-long neck femoral heads showed increased wear compared with medium necks, with metal heads affected more than ceramic ones. Although no serious damage occurred in testing, these findings suggest longer necks may have greater wear potential in hip replacements.

articles.title: Single versus dual antibiotic-loaded bone cement in hip fracture arthroplasty: a cohort study of 56,434 hip arthroplasties from the Dutch Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Yoon SJ, Van Marle L, Van Steenbergen LN, Bos PK, Jutte PC, Wouthuyzen-Bakker M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing cemented hip arthroplasty for hip fracture
articles.sample_size: 56,434 hip arthroplasties (1,651 with dual antibiotic cement, remainder with single antibiotic cement)
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, revision for infection, and mortality at 1 year and beyond
articles.take_home: Using dual antibiotic-loaded cement instead of single antibiotic cement did not reduce the need for revision surgery in hip fracture patients, and was actually associated with a slightly higher revision rate for infection and increased mortality. Single antibiotic cement appears to be as effective as dual antibiotic cement for this procedure.

articles.title: Smart Implantable Device Use is Associated with Decreased Post-Discharge Hospital Utilization in Total Knee Arthroplasty Patients Who Have Metabolic Syndrome: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.authors: Nakla A, Aubin PM, Ademisoye S, Burr RG, Rajaee SS, Wu M
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 1,562 total knee arthroplasties (142 with smart implantable device, 1,420 without)
articles.outcomes: Emergency department visits within 90 days, hospital readmissions within 90 days, and medical complications
articles.take_home: Patients with metabolic syndrome who received a smart implantable device with their knee replacement had fewer emergency department visits (9.9% versus 16.6%) and fewer readmissions (5.6% versus 11.1%) in the first 90 days after surgery compared to those without the device. Those without the device also had higher rates of medical complications.

articles.title: Functional Limb Length Preservation and Coronal Alignment Categories in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Khury F, Ehlers M, Aziz HH, Sarfraz A, Meftah M, Schwarzkopf R
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Functional limb length preservation, coronal alignment, KOOS JR scores, PROMIS pain intensity and pain interference at 3 months and 1 year
articles.take_home: Revision knee replacement preserved leg length and alignment in about two-thirds of patients. Over-lengthening the leg slightly and preserving the original knee angle were associated with better early pain relief, though all patients showed similar improvement by one year.

articles.title: Association of joint line changes with patient-reported outcomes after cruciate-retaining robotic arm-assisted total knee arthroplasty with functional alignment.
articles.authors: Jung HJ, Cha SH, Hwang J, Kim JI
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary cruciate-retaining robotic arm-assisted total knee replacement with functional alignment
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes at 1 year after surgery, measured using the Forgotten Joint Score-12
articles.take_home: When the joint line is lifted on the inner side of the knee during robotic-assisted knee replacement, patients report worse outcomes at one year. A small drop in the joint line on either side of the knee appears to be acceptable and does not harm patient satisfaction.

articles.title: Coronal stability at mid-stance is preserved in mechanically aligned medial pivot total knee arthroplasty despite intraoperative lateral laxity.
articles.authors: Soeno T, Sato T, Kobayashi K, Katsumi R, Kawashima H
articles.population: Patients undergoing mechanically aligned medial pivot total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Coronal alignment and joint stability during mid-stance phase of gait, including femoral-tibial varus-valgus angle, mediolateral displacement, and femoral condylar lift-off
articles.take_home: Knees with medial pivot design showed stable alignment during walking despite having some looseness on the outer side of the knee during surgery. The knees remained properly aligned when patients walked, with minimal unwanted movement and no signs of instability.

articles.title: Modular intramedullary knee arthrodesis for chronic periprosthetic joint infection after total knee arthroplasty: Patient-reported satisfaction and functional outcomes.
articles.authors: Corti J, Raspanti F, Secci G, Giabbani N, Piccica M, Mugnaini M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with chronic periprosthetic joint infection after total knee arthroplasty treated with knee arthrodesis
articles.outcomes: Infection recurrence, mechanical failure, patient satisfaction, walking ability, quality of life (SF-12 physical and mental component scores), living independently
articles.take_home: Knee arthrodesis using a special intramedullary nail successfully controlled infection and prevented mechanical failure in all 15 patients, with 73% satisfied and all preferring this procedure to amputation. Most patients remained able to walk with aids and lived independently, though younger patients had better physical quality of life scores.

articles.title: Clinical and radiographic outcomes after fixation of posterior cruciate ligament tibial avulsion fractures using a modified anterior tension band construct.
articles.authors: Oner SK, Kuyubasi SN, Kozlu S, Ocak B, Batak U, Kestel S
articles.population: Patients with posterior cruciate ligament tibial avulsion fractures treated with open reduction and internal fixation
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union, knee flexion range of motion, Lysholm and IKDC scores, complications, return-to-activity
articles.take_home: All fractures healed successfully using a modified surgical technique with two screws and a wire construct, with patients achieving good knee movement and functional scores. However, the study cannot confirm this method is better than standard screw fixation alone as there was no comparison group.

articles.title: Risk factors for wound complications in direct anterior total hip arthroplasty: a 10-year analysis.
articles.authors: Schaffler BC, Haider M, Manjunath A, Richardson M, Davidovitch R, Hepinstall M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing direct anterior total hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 725 patients from five surgeons over 10 years (2011-2023)
articles.outcomes: Wound complications (11.4% of patients). Risk factors identified: higher body mass index, longer surgery time, less experienced surgeons, and use of negative pressure wound therapy. Patients with wound complications had higher rates of infection, emergency visits, readmission and revision surgery.
articles.take_home: This study found that patients with higher body weight, longer operations and less experienced surgeons were more likely to develop wound problems after hip replacement through the direct anterior approach. Using special wound dressings (negative pressure therapy) did not prevent these complications and was actually associated with more problems.

articles.title: Acetabular fracture open reduction and internal fixation in patients under 60: time to total hip arthroplasty and implant survivorship: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Cheruvu MS, Narayana Murthy S, Ford D, Singh R, Okoro T, Steele N
articles.population: Patients under 60 years old who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for acetabular fracture and later required total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Time from initial fracture repair to hip replacement (mean 5.2 years), implant survival rates at 5, 10 and 15 years, and complication rates including dislocation, infection and reoperation
articles.take_home: In younger patients with acetabular fractures, initial surgery to repair the fracture typically delays the need for hip replacement by about 5 years, though between a quarter and a third eventually need this conversion surgery. The replacement implants work well initially but do have higher complication rates than standard hip replacements.

articles.title: Anatomical versus reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for primary glenohumeral osteoarthritis with an intact rotator cuff : a systematic review.
articles.authors: Shah PP, Jayawardena R, Wong R, Poff C, Maassen NH, Shi L
articles.population: Patients with glenohumeral osteoarthritis and an intact rotator cuff
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, patient-reported outcomes, complications, revisions, cost, radiological changes, and satisfaction
articles.take_home: Anatomical and reverse total shoulder arthroplasty produce similar overall results for osteoarthritis with an intact rotator cuff. Anatomical surgery may give slightly better movement, but reverse surgery appears to be a reasonable alternative option.

articles.title: Isolated versus Full-Component Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Aseptic Loosening: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Sheth N, McCall M, Hrudka B, Syed O, Brito M, Seilern J, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty for aseptic loosening
articles.sample_size: 11 studies with median 164 cases per study; mean age 66 years; 65.8% women
articles.outcomes: Re-revision rates, implant failures, complications (aseptic loosening and periprosthetic joint infection), operative time, blood loss, and postoperative range of motion
articles.take_home: Replacing just the loose component of a knee replacement performed as well as replacing all components, with the advantage of shorter surgery time. Isolated component revision may be a less damaging option when the other parts of the replacement are still well-fixed.

articles.title: Collared Stems Are Associated With Reduced Early Aseptic Loosening and All-Cause Revision Rate.
articles.authors: Oettl FC, Dimitriou D, Zingg PO, Hoch A
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national registry data
articles.population: Patients aged 50 years and over undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 168,493 primary THAs (143,427 non-collared stems, 25,066 collared stems)
articles.outcomes: Revision for aseptic femoral loosening and all-cause revision rates at 10-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Hip replacements with collared stems had better long-term survival, with a 42% lower risk of loosening and 35% lower risk of needing revision surgery compared to non-collared stems. This suggests collared stem design may be beneficial for hip replacement outcomes in osteoarthritis patients.

articles.title: Morphological and functional variability of ramp lesions influences surgical management during anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A national registry study of the French Arthroscopic Society.
articles.authors: Noailles T, Bouguennec N, Hardy A, Cavaignac E, Common H, Labarre C, et al.
articles.study_type: Multicentre descriptive study using prospective registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with an associated ramp lesion
articles.outcomes: Association between Thaunat classification of ramp lesions, meniscal mobility patterns, and surgical repair strategy; repair technique used and number of sutures needed
articles.take_home: Ramp lesions vary in shape and size and are associated with different patterns of abnormal knee movement, which influences how surgeons decide to repair them. Most surgeons in France repaired these lesions using a hook technique through a specific surgical approach, with the type of lesion determining how many stitches were needed.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of advanced knee orthosis designs in managing knee osteoarthritis: A systematic review of biomechanical and clinical outcomes.
articles.authors: Zangi M, Taheri M, Mahmoodi S, Nikkho B, Khosravi M
articles.study_type: Systematic review of knee orthosis designs
articles.population: Adults with knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: Eleven studies with approximately 300 participants total
articles.outcomes: Knee adduction moment reduction, pain reduction, gait improvement, strength and function, progression to knee replacement surgery, and symptom scores
articles.take_home: Pneumatic knee braces show the strongest evidence for helping with knee osteoarthritis, reducing pain by up to 36% and improving walking and strength. Vibratory and magnetic braces may also help, though the evidence is less strong, and larger high-quality studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Factors associated with rotational alignment on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging in patients with anterior cruciate ligament injury.
articles.authors: Mochizuki H, Kikuchi N, Tsutsumi R, Okamoto C, Kanamori A, Terajima S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament injury
articles.outcomes: Factors associated with tibial internal rotation on preoperative MRI, including sex, lateral posterior tibial slope, and ligament injuries
articles.take_home: Men and patients with a steeper slope on the outer back of the tibia are more likely to have increased inward rotation of the tibia when assessed on MRI before ACL surgery. This finding may help identify patients at higher risk of graft failure after ACL reconstruction.

articles.title: Risk factors for failure following debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) in early periprosthetic joint infection after primary total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Campos RS, Cavalcanti AS, Jader Batista de Almeida H Jr, Perini JA, Fernandes MBC, Arruda de Matos J
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty between January 2011 and December 2017, developed early periprosthetic joint infection, and were treated with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention with minimum 1 year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Success rate of DAIR treatment; identification of risk factors for infection persistence, recrudescence, recurrence, or need for revision surgery
articles.take_home: DAIR surgery to treat early hip infection after hip replacement was successful in about 72 out of every 100 cases. Patients with low blood haemoglobin levels before surgery and longer operating times had worse outcomes, whilst patients with fewer other health conditions and osteoarthritis as the original reason for hip replacement did better.

articles.title: Incidence and risk factors for postoperative myocardial infarction following hip and knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Al-Saadawi A, Gill SS, Sousi S, Jones GG, Bottle A, Cobb JP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using linked hospital and mortality data
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip or knee arthroplasty in England between January 1998 and March 2021
articles.outcomes: Incidence of myocardial infarction at 30, 90, and 365 days after surgery; MI-related mortality
articles.take_home: Heart attacks after hip and knee replacement are uncommon, occurring in less than 0.4% of patients within a year, but when they do happen they carry serious mortality risk. Bone-sparing procedures like hip resurfacing and partial knee replacement had lower rates of heart attacks than standard full replacements.

articles.title: Comparison of Postoperative Outcomes Following Simultaneous versus Staged Bilateral Total Knee Arthroplasty in Obese Patients: A Database Study.
articles.authors: Patel D, Gay S, Belzile E, Barimani B, Albers A, Mutch J
articles.population: Adults undergoing bilateral total knee arthroplasty, stratified by obesity class and surgical timing
articles.sample_size: 11,965 patients (5,653 non-obese; 3,096 class 1 obesity; 1,870 class 2 obesity; 1,346 class 3 obesity)
articles.outcomes: 30-day composite complications, readmission, length of stay, two-year aseptic loosening and all-cause revision
articles.take_home: In obese patients (BMI 35 or above), having both knees replaced in separate procedures staged several weeks or months apart led to fewer complications and revision surgeries at two years compared with simultaneous bilateral surgery, with the greatest benefits seen in patients with the highest BMI. In non-obese patients, staged procedures were associated with higher early readmission rates.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in the Utilization of Robotic-Assisted Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.authors: Ogu E, Valencia A, Sambandam S
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years or older undergoing total hip arthroplasty in the United States between January 2014 and February 2026
articles.outcomes: Odds of undergoing robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty (RA-THA) across racial and ethnic groups
articles.take_home: Minority patients, particularly Black and African American patients, were significantly less likely to receive robotic-assisted hip replacement compared with White patients, and these differences persisted even after accounting for clinical and demographic factors, suggesting structural barriers rather than medical reasons are responsible.

articles.title: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with concomitant all-inside lateral meniscus posterior root repair shows comparable graft survivorship and clinical outcomes to isolated ACL reconstruction.
articles.authors: Carrozzo A, Berard E, Petrini T, Ben Roummane H, Geiger M, Pailhe R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction between January 2017 and December 2023
articles.sample_size: 841 knees (786 isolated ACLR, 55 ACLR with lateral meniscus posterior root repair)
articles.outcomes: ACL graft rerupture-free survival, return to sport, return to work, contralateral ACL rupture, and knee function at 12 months
articles.take_home: Adding lateral meniscus posterior root repair to ACL reconstruction surgery does not reduce graft survival or worsen clinical outcomes compared to ACL reconstruction alone. Both groups showed similar rates of graft failure and functional recovery at 24-46 months of follow-up.

articles.title: Rectus femoris tendon autograft yields comparable early outcomes to hamstring tendon autograft, but evidence remains limited: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Ge Y, Haner M, Borges JS, Tang J, Stockle U, Petersen W
articles.study_type: Systematic review of comparative clinical studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary or revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with rectus femoris tendon or hamstring tendon autografts
articles.sample_size: 324 patients enrolled; 299 available for analysis (142 rectus femoris, 157 hamstring)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes (International Knee Documentation Committee and Tegner scores), quadriceps strength (peak torque), graft failure rates, and donor-site morbidity
articles.take_home: Rectus femoris tendon grafts produce similar early results to hamstring tendon grafts for knee ligament reconstruction, though the evidence is limited to only four small studies. Rectus femoris may be useful as an alternative when standard grafts are not available, particularly in repeat surgery, but cannot yet be recommended as a routine first choice.

articles.title: MRI-based deep learning models match or surpass physician performance for early detection and staging of avascular necrosis of the femoral head: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Skaik K, Abdallah JP, Bouchard MD, Ayeni OR, Almasri M
articles.study_type: Systematic review of deep learning studies
articles.population: Patients with avascular necrosis of the femoral head undergoing MRI
articles.sample_size: 10 studies included; 1054 patients for early detection, 1573 for staging, 276 for both
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and AUROC for early detection and staging of avascular necrosis; comparison of deep learning model performance versus physician performance
articles.take_home: Deep learning models using MRI scans performed as well as experienced doctors and better than less experienced ones at detecting and staging avascular necrosis of the hip. These computer-based tools could help improve diagnosis reliability in this difficult area of imaging.

articles.title: Clinical improvement despite structural degeneration after nonoperative treatment of medial meniscus posterior root tear: A prospective longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Nonaka S, Hatayama K, Okada K, Kakiage H, Terauchi M, Chikuda H
articles.population: Adults with acute medial meniscus posterior root tear managed without surgery
articles.outcomes: Clinical pain and function improved significantly within 6 months, but structural changes in the knee (cartilage loss, joint space narrowing, meniscus extrusion) worsened. 23.4% of patients chose surgery after a median of 6 months, more often those with greater varus (inward) knee alignment.
articles.take_home: Most patients with this type of meniscus tear improved clinically with nonoperative treatment despite their knee showing structural deterioration on imaging. Patients with more inward-angled knees were more likely to eventually choose surgery.

articles.title: Autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cell injection for knee osteoarthritis improves pain and function without a clear increase in adverse events: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Han JH, Jung M, Chung K, Moon HS, Jung SH, Baik SH, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Pain (visual analogue scale), function (WOMAC scores), adverse events and serious adverse events
articles.take_home: Injections of cells from patients' own fat tissue improved pain and function in knee osteoarthritis at 3, 6 and 12 months compared with control treatment, without a clear increase in harmful effects. However, the evidence is limited by differences between studies and lack of long-term follow-up data.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based axial-plane analysis of lower extremity torsion with dedicated 3D planning software is reliable and efficient.
articles.authors: Lippuner J, Huttner F, Ferner F, Sinha D, Weyer-Elberich V, Vogt B, et al.
articles.population: Healthy volunteers
articles.sample_size: 100 people (50 male, 50 female), mean age 26.7 years
articles.outcomes: Reliability and efficiency of 3D planning software for measuring leg bone angles on MRI compared with manual measurement. Inter and intraobserver reliability assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Measurement times recorded.
articles.take_home: Dedicated 3D planning software reliably measures leg bone angles from MRI scans with good to very good accuracy, comparable to manual measurement. The software was faster to use, particularly for less experienced doctors, saving about 25% of measurement time.

articles.title: Simultaneous and staged bilateral medial opening wedge high tibial osteotomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Duru DO, Mussie E, Degen RM, Litchfield RB, Sehgol TA
articles.population: Adults undergoing bilateral medial opening wedge high tibial osteotomy for varus knee malalignment
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures, radiographic alignment (medial proximal tibial angle and posterior tibial slope), hospital stay, and complications including infection rates
articles.take_home: Both having both knee operations at once or in separate operations improved patients' symptoms and knee alignment similarly well. Having both operations together meant shorter total hospital stay, but the choice between approaches should be tailored to each patient's health and recovery capacity.

articles.title: Influence of visualization portal selection on femoral tunnel placement and anterior knee pain after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Altuntas Y, Ipek E, Balkanli B, Alibakan G, Bozca MA, Eren OT
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 184 patients (90 central transpatellar portal, 94 anteromedial portal)
articles.outcomes: Femoral tunnel angle, femoral tunnel height and depth ratios, tibial tunnel angle, anterior knee pain (VAS scores), and knee function (Kujala scores) at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months
articles.take_home: Using an anteromedial portal for viewing during ACL reconstruction surgery resulted in less anterior knee pain and better early function at 3 months compared to a central transpatellar portal. However, by 12 months and beyond, both approaches produced similar results, suggesting the early advantage does not translate to long-term differences.

articles.title: Occupational hazards in hip and knee adult reconstruction surgery : a systematic review of physical and psychological stressors.
articles.authors: Innocenti M, Civinini R, Leggieri F, Lustig S, Batailler C, van Laarhoven SN, et al.
articles.population: Surgeons performing hip and knee joint replacement surgery
articles.sample_size: 38 studies included (individual study sample sizes not specified)
articles.outcomes: Work-related injury prevalence, noise exposure levels, hearing loss rates, physiological demands, ergonomic strain, and impact of robotic-assisted surgery
articles.take_home: Surgeons performing hip and knee replacements face high rates of work-related injuries (66-96.5%) and hearing loss (31% versus 11% in non-surgical staff), with particularly demanding procedures generating noise levels of 77-88 decibels. Robotic assistance can improve some ergonomic factors but increases operating time and noise levels, so comprehensive workplace health strategies are needed to protect surgeons' long-term wellbeing.

articles.title: Tibial implant migration of cemented and cementless total and unicompartmental knee arthroplasties in patients with low and normal bone mineral density: a 5-year RSA cohort study of 397 cases.
articles.authors: Linde KN, Langdahl BL, Rytter S, Nelissen RGHH, Stilling M
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with radiostereometry follow-up
articles.population: Patients undergoing unicompartmental or total knee arthroplasty with cemented or cementless implants
articles.outcomes: Tibial implant migration measured by radiostereometry at 1, 2 and 5 years; maximum total point motion differences between low and normal bone mineral density groups
articles.take_home: Tibial implant migration was similar in patients with low and normal bone mineral density, regardless of whether implants were cemented or not. The researchers note their findings are limited by small group sizes and wide confidence intervals, so more research is needed to understand the role of bone density in implant migration.

articles.title: Comparative study of core decompression with allograft and autologous bone marrow therapy plus alendronate versus classical bone graft alone in Ficat grade II-III avascular necrosis of the hip.
articles.authors: Alkhuzai A
articles.population: Adults with Ficat Grade II-III avascular necrosis of the hip
articles.outcomes: Pain and function assessed using WOMAC, Harris Hip Score and Oxford Hip Score at 6, 12 and 24 months; necrotic area size on MRI
articles.take_home: Patients treated with core decompression using stem cells and allograft bone plus a bone-strengthening medication showed better pain relief, movement and function than those treated with core decompression and traditional bone graft alone over two years. The stem cell approach also reduced the size of the dead bone area more effectively.

articles.title: The association between spinopelvic alignment and non-traumatic femoral head AVN: a case-control radiographic study.
articles.authors: Aktan C, Kati YA, Ayhan Z, Kosar A, Ergun M, Guler F
articles.population: Adults with non-traumatic avascular necrosis of the femoral head and age- and sex-matched asymptomatic controls
articles.outcomes: Sagittal spinopelvic parameters including pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, lumbar lordosis, thoracic kyphosis, and sagittal vertical axis
articles.take_home: Patients with avascular necrosis of the hip had different spinal and pelvic alignment compared to people without the condition, with reduced measurements in several key angles. This altered alignment may affect how stress is distributed through the hip joint, though more research is needed to understand if this is related to how avascular necrosis develops.

articles.title: Hip resurfacing: a narrative review of the past, present and future.
articles.authors: Filer J, Baker RP
articles.population: Hip resurfacing arthroplasty patients
articles.outcomes: Historical design concepts, bearing materials, current indications, patient selection criteria, modern prosthesis development
articles.take_home: This review examines how hip resurfacing surgery has evolved over time, showing how past successes and failures have guided which patients should receive this treatment today and what types of implants work best.

articles.title: Risk factors for avascular necrosis in Delbet type II paediatric femoral neck fractures: a case-control study.
articles.authors: Gopinathan NR, Ghosh AK, Khatri JP, Rangasamy K, Ksheerasagar VP, Sudesh P
articles.population: Children with Delbet type II paediatric femoral neck fractures
articles.sample_size: 15 fractures (5 cases with avascular necrosis, 10 controls without)
articles.outcomes: Avascular necrosis development; functional outcomes assessed by Ratliff criteria and modified Harris Hip Score at mean 35.2 months follow-up
articles.take_home: An increased angle of the broken bone after surgery was the main predictor of avascular necrosis in this type of hip fracture in children. When avascular necrosis did develop, most children had good functional outcomes with 12 months of bone-strengthening medication and restricted weight-bearing.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional total hip arthroplasty in Crowe Type 3-4 developmental dysplasia of the hip: a single-centre retrospective comparative cohort study.
articles.authors: Kezer M, Turan K, Camurcu IY, Ak S, Gultekin O
articles.population: Patients with Crowe type 3-4 developmental dysplasia of the hip undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Radiographic accuracy of cup placement, Harris Hip Score, leg-length discrepancy, operative time, and complications
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted and conventional hip replacement produced similar clinical results and complication rates in severe hip dysplasia, although the robotic procedure took longer to perform. Further larger studies are needed to confirm whether the robotic approach offers long-term benefits.

articles.title: Distinct recovery phenotypes after hip arthroscopy reveal dissociation between daily function and sports performance.
articles.authors: Vazquez M, Seijas R, Alvarez-Diaz P, Laiz P, Escutia-Mari L, Ferre-Aniorte A, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study with machine learning analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement
articles.outcomes: Hip Outcome Score activities of daily living and sports performance subscales at 1 year; identification of 4 recovery phenotypes
articles.take_home: After hip arthroscopy, patients follow four different recovery patterns. About 27% recover well for everyday activities but struggle with sports, which is more likely if they are over 40, were not very active before surgery, or had significant cartilage damage.

articles.title: What causes cup inclination outliers in primary total hip arthroplasty when using a digital inclinometer? A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Meermans G, Van Doorn WJ, Kats JJ, Innmann M, Grammatopoulos G
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Achievement of target cup inclination angle (35-45 degrees) measured by radiography; accuracy of digital inclinometer guidance; factors associated with outliers
articles.take_home: A digital inclinometer helped surgeons position the hip cup within 3 degrees of their target in 93% of cases, though only 74% ended up in the ideal 35-45 degree range on X-rays. Most cups that fell outside the target range were due to the patient's pelvis moving during surgery rather than surgeon error.

articles.title: Peak stresses within the cement mantle increase above the yield point of bone cement when the subsidence limit is reached in polished taper stems.
articles.authors: Taufiqurrakhman M, Jones A, Abdullah AH, Higgins M, Bloch BV, Manktelow ARJ, et al.
articles.population: Three commonly used polished taper-slip hip stem designs
articles.outcomes: Peak stress within cement mantle and stress distribution when subsidence is restricted
articles.take_home: When hip replacement stems cannot move down as much as designed, stress in the cement mantle increases significantly (by up to twice as much), particularly at the stem tip, which may increase the risk of fracture around the implant.

articles.title: Outcomes with use of a modular, cementless, tapered and fluted femoral prosthesis in revision hip arthroplasty with mid-term follow-up.
articles.authors: Hughes C, Lim B, Morrison SR, Akhtar MA, Walmsley P, Ballantyne JA
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 125 procedures, 100 with at least 2 years follow-up
articles.outcomes: Implant survival, aseptic loosening, stem migration, reoperation rate, mobility restoration, intraoperative complications
articles.take_home: The Link MP stem showed excellent survival (96% at 166 months) with low rates of stem-related reoperation (4%). Most patients returned to baseline mobility, and early stem migration did not affect function, though infection and mechanical issues at the joint required some patients to return to theatre.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of locked and unlocked blade proximal femoral nail antirotation implants in the treatment of trochanteric fractures based on reduction quality and clinical success criteria.
articles.authors: Cicek AC, Yildiz V
articles.population: Patients aged over 65 years with trochanteric fractures
articles.outcomes: Reduction quality, operation time, intraoperative bleeding, radiological measurements, postoperative complications, Harris Hip Score, Visual Analog Scale pain scores
articles.take_home: Both types of nail implant worked similarly well overall for hip fractures in older patients, but unlocked blade implants took less time to insert, caused less bleeding during surgery, and had fewer complications. Long-term pain relief and hip function were comparable between the two types.
